As a Manufacturing Engineer, you are responsible for developing and maintaining methods, operating sequences, and processes in the fabrication of parts, components, subassemblies, and final assemblies. You'll work closely with other engineering functions to coordinate the release of product improvements and new products, and you'll use engineering principles to estimate and reduce manufacturing costs, improve product quality, determine time standards, and make recommendations for tooling and process requirements. Your expertise in lean principles, automation, and continuous improvement will be instrumental in driving operational excellence and achieving higher levels of productivity and cost-effectiveness. You'll develop and use test procedures, evaluate test results, and assess work methods, procedures, and policies to identify root cause issues and solutions that ensure operational success.

Role Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain all methods, operating sequences, and processes in the fabrication of parts, components, subassemblies, and final assemblies 
  • Work with other engineering functions to coordinate the release of product improvements and new products 
  • Use basic engineering and design for excellence (DFx) principles to estimate and reduce manufacturing and/or product costs, and to improve product quality 
  • Determine time standards, and make recommendations for tooling and process requirements 
  • Develop and use test procedures, evaluate test results, and evaluate work methods, procedures, and policies   
  • Determine root causes and corrective actions for issues that arise during assembly or system testing; perform Process Failure Mode & Effects Analysis; and provide reports as needed 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 2-4 years of related experience

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong conceptual knowledge and technical experience for everyday problem-solving on the job   
  • Solid interpersonal skills, and the ability to clearly explain complex information to others

This position may require standing for extended periods of time, walking, working in tight spaces, bending, squatting, twisting, kneeling, reaching, lifting, the ability to distinguish between colors, the ability to work in an environment with noise that may be difficult for some individuals with sensitivity to noise, and the use of hand and power tools. Job Description

As a Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer here at Honeywell, you will lead initiatives to optimize and innovate manufacturing processes, driving operational excellence and efficiency. You will leverage your expertise to implement advanced manufacturing strategies and technologies that enhance productivity and product quality.

The Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer will be responsible for developing, implementing, validating, maintaining, and improving manufacturing processes across machining, assembly, test, fabrication, and engineered plastics operations. This role supports the production of centrifugal pump components, including machined metallic components and ANSIMAG sealless magnetic-drive non-metallic product lines with molded ETFE wetted components.

The successful candidate will lead continuous improvement, cost reduction, quality improvement, and production support initiatives by partnering closely with shop-floor technicians, operators, supervisors, Product Engineering, Planning, Quality, Supply Chain, and management. This is a day-shift, salaried position that works under limited supervision and reports to the Shop Supervisor / Manager. You’ll work out of our Arvada, CO location on an On-site work schedule.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, validate, maintain, and improve manufacturing processes for assigned areas, including machining, assembly, test, kit fabrication, engineered plastic parts, insert molded parts, and injection molded fabrication processes
  • Create, revise, and maintain NC programs, fixturing, tooling, standard work, process sketches, in-process inspection plans, process notes, assembly instructions, process instructions, test instructions, bills of material, labor routings, and shop-floor routings
  • Evaluate alternative plastic resins, manufacturing methods, equipment, tooling, and process improvements to support cost reduction, manufacturability, quality, and product performance
  • Improve manufacturing efficiency by analyzing workflow, production flow, assembly methods, space requirements, equipment layout, process capability, and production volume while maintaining and improving quality standards
  • Lead analysis of manufacturing costs in support of strategic make/buy decisions, accurate standard costing, capital investment justification, and cost-reduction initiatives
  • Participate in production traceability and configuration control, including changes and corrections to bills of material, routings, technical work instructions, NC programs, inspection plans, and test plans
  • Support non-conforming material disposition, root cause analysis, customer complaint investigations, internal issue resolution, third-party audit responses, and corrective action implementation
  • Lead and support Lean, Six Sigma, TPM, and 5S initiatives to eliminate waste, reduce variation, remove bottlenecks, and improve manufacturing, assembly, test, and fabrication processes
  • Coordinate with Manufacturing Supervision, operators, technicians, engineers, Quality, Supply Chain, Planning, and management to resolve production issues and improve manufacturing capabilities
  • Support injection molding training and develop working knowledge of internal processes, customer specifications, and best practices for sealless magnetic-drive pump products
  • Identify, justify, research, quote, procure, test, and implement capital equipment investments, including preparation of Capital Authorization Requests as needed

Qualifications

You Must Have:

  • 5+ years of experience in a manufacturing engineering or similar role within a manufacturing environment
  • 3+ years of experience with CAD/CAM software; Siemens NX preferred
  • 3+ years of experience in machining, metal cutting, plastics manufacturing, injection molding, or related production environment
  • Experience with varied metallurgies such as carbon steel, stainless steel alloys, titanium, Hastelloy, and aluminum preferred
  • Experience supporting engineered plastic components, molded ETFE components, insert molded parts, or injection molded fabrication processes preferred
  • Ability to lift 35 pounds unassisted

We Value

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related field
  • Lean Six Sigma experience, APICS certification, or demonstrated experience applying lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies
  • Experience with VPP sites, EH&S programs, TPM, 6S, ISO standard work, and formal safety management practices
  • Experience managing multi-shift or 24-hour machine shop operations
  • Familiarity with various production processes, including plastic molding, tooling, assembly, and test
  • Strong communication skills, reading, listening, and talking are common
